Also compare quote hours to the job routing estimate to see whether the routing or the quote carries the padding. Check work_date truncation is irrelevant (hours summed per op, not per day). Part 2: among decided NEW quotes (won/lost/expired/no award), compute est_hours per $ of est_material (and labour share of quoted price) and test hit rate across quintiles, within customer segment and year, and within customer (customer-demeaned).", "support": "Quote-stage actual/estimate pooled below ~0.9 at laser, brake, mill, lathe, paint, assembly but ~1 at weld; AND hit rate declining monotonically across hours-per-material-dollar quintiles, persisting within year/segment/customer.", "weaken": "Quote-stage hours match actuals (ratio ~1) even though routings don't; or hit rate flat across labour intensity quintiles or the gradient disappears within customer/year; or ratio depends on matching artefacts.", "expect": "Moderate confidence that quote-stage ratios are below 1 outside weld (routing likely derived from quote). input.sql:
WITH l AS (
  SELECT q.quote_id, ql.quote_line_id, ql.part_id, ql.quantity qq, j.job_id, j.quantity jq
  FROM erp_sales_orders so JOIN erp_quotes q ON q.quote_id=so.quote_id
  JOIN erp_so_lines sl ON sl.order_id=so.order_id
  JOIN erp_quote_lines ql ON ql.quote_id=q.quote_id AND ql.part_id=sl.part_id
  JOIN erp_jobs j ON j.line_id=sl.line_id AND j.kind='order'
  WHERE j.completed_on IS NOT NULL),
ops AS (
  SELECT o.job_id, o.work_centre, sum(o.est_setup_hours+o.est_run_hours) est_job, sum(coalesce(la.h,0)) act
  FROM erp_job_operations o LEFT JOIN (SELECT op_id, sum(hours) h FROM shop_labour_entries GROUP BY op_id) la USING(op_id)
  GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT ops.work_centre, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT l.job_id) jobs,
 round(sum(ops.act),0) act_h, round(sum(h.setup_hours+h.run_hours*l.jq),0) quote_h, round(sum(ops.est_job),0) route_h,
 round(sum(ops.act)/sum(h.setup_hours+h.run_hours*l.jq),3) act_over_quote,
 round(sum(ops.act)/sum(ops.est_job),3) act_over_route,
 round(sum(ops.est_job)/sum(h.setup_hours+h.run_hours*l.jq),3) route_over_quote,
 round(median(ops.act/nullif(h.setup_hours+h.run_hours*l.jq,0)),3) med_act_quote,
 sum(CASE WHEN l.jq=l.qq THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) same_qty
FROM l JOIN ops ON ops.job_id=l.job_id
JOIN erp_quote_line_hours h ON h.quote_line_id=l.quote_line_id AND h.work_centre=ops.work_centre
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

ops AS (
  SELECT o.job_id, o.work_centre, o.est_setup_hours+o.est_run_hours est, coalesce(la.h,0) act

   sum(ql.est_hours) h, sum(ql.est_material) m, sum(ql.unit_price*ql.quantity) val
  FROM erp_quotes q JOIN erp_quote_lines ql USING(quote_id)
  WHERE q.kind='new' AND q.status IN ('won','lost','expired','no award')

 round(avg(CASE WHEN status='lost' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),4) lost_rate,
 round(median(val),0) med_val
FROM b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

input.content:
# H4 notes
- q257: quote line layout; run_hours per piece, est_material is line total, unit_price per piece.
- q261: key-linked won NEW quotes (sales_orders.quote_id) -> job on same part. Job routing est == quote est (setup + run/pc x qty) exactly at every WC (route_over_quote 1.000), job qty == quote qty on all. Actual/quote >=1 everywhere except lathe 0.942 (117 ops): laser 1.009, brake 1.024, mill 1.052, paint 1.066, assembly 1.128, weld 1.277. Premise of H4 fails for new parts.
- q265: the low ratios (~0.72-0.87, orient q80) come from REPEAT jobs: actual/est falls with nth job of part (laser 0.958 -> 0.739, brake 1.001 -> 0.741, weld 1.223 -> 0.917; inspect flat ~1.06). Learning curve on unchanged routing. Caveat: "first job in data" may not be first ever for parts made before 2016.
- q268: non-weld first-job ratio 1.01-1.079 every year; weld 1.215-1.329, drifting up.
- q266/q267/q270: hit rate does NOT fall with hours per $ material; Q1 0.2224 vs Q5 0.265; within customer-year slope +0.0143 (corr 0.0199). Non-material share: flat 0.2356-0.2653. Dead end for the pricing->hit-rate link.
- work_date truncation irrelevant: hours summed per op.
- Side finding: weld underestimated on new parts by ~1,004.5 h/yr on key-linked sample only (q271).

content.text:
H4 doesn't hold, so I saved F7 with `dollars_a_year` left null (it can't be sized). Neither half of the hypothesis survives.

**1. New-part quotes are not over-estimated.** I matched won new quotes to their first job through the 2,764 orders that carry a quote id. The job routing is copied straight from the quote (routing ÷ quote = 1.000 at every work centre), and actual hours come in at or above it (q261):

| Work centre | Actual ÷ quoted hours | Operations |
|---|---|---|
| laser | 1.009 | 5,118 |
| brake | 1.024 | 3,788 |
| mill | 1.052 | 333 |
| paint | 1.066 | 3,663 |
| assembly | 1.128 | 1,043 |
| weld | 1.277 | 2,373 |
| lathe | 0.942 | 117 |

Lathe is the only one under, on a small sample. The pattern holds in every year: outside weld 1.01–1.079, weld 1.215–1.329 and rising (q268). The posting-date problem with `work_date` doesn't affect this, because I summed hours per operation, not per day.

**2. Where the low overall ratios (0.72–0.87) come from.** It's repeat jobs. Actual ÷ estimate falls each time a part is run again: laser goes from 0.958 on its first job to 0.739 after the 11th, brake from 1.001 to 0.741 (q265). My reading is a learning curve on routings that never get updated, but that's an interpretation. One caveat: for parts made before 2016, the first job in the records may not be the first one ever run.

**3. Hit rate doesn't fall as quotes get more labour-heavy.** Across 10,948 decided new quotes (372 customers), I split them into fifths by estimated hours per material dollar. The lowest fifth wins 0.2224 and the highest wins 0.265, so labour-heavy quotes win slightly more, not less (q266). Within the same customer and year the relationship is essentially zero (slope +0.0143, correlation 0.0199, q267). By the non-material share of the quoted price, hit rate is flat at 0.2356–0.2653 (q270).

**What's worth acting on instead:**
- **Weld is under-quoted on new parts.** On the 2,764 key-linked orders, actual weld hours run 1,004.5 hours a year over the quote (q271).
